forecast-period.text: A cold front will move across the south of the state today, clearing the east of the state in the afternoon. Another ridge of high pressure will follow on Thursday, with another cold front clipping the southeast on Friday. Another high moves over waters to the south of SA on Saturday.
For latest warnings go to www.bom.gov.au, subscribe to RSS feeds, call 1300 659 210* or listen for warnings on relevant TV and radio broadcasts.
* Calls to 1300 numbers cost around 27.5c incl. GST, higher from mobiles or public phones.

Showers extending across the agricultural areas, with possible thunderstorms about the South East and the far eastern Riverland and Murraylands. Maximum temperatures above average in the northeast grading to below average elsewhere. Light winds tending northwesterly ahead of a fresh and gusty southwest to southerly change extending throughout the day.

Possible light morning showers about windward coast and ranges. Maximum temperatures generally below average. Generally southwest to southeasterly winds, fresh and gusty in the northeast during the morning.

Showers about windward coasts, extending across the southern agricultural area from late morning. Maximum temperatures below average about the southern agricultural area, grading to above average in the north and west. Light winds, shifting north to northwesterly ahead of a fresh southwest to southeasterly change extending throughout during the afternoon and evening.

text.p: Dry apart from possible showers or thunderstorms in the west. Maximum temperatures above average in the west and far north grading to below average elsewhere. Moderate to fresh southwest to southeasterly winds, shifting east to northeasterly in the west.

Cumulative rainfall totals to the end of Saturday: less than 2 mm about the northern agricultural area and in the west, increasing to 2 to 10 mm across the southern agricultural area, with possible falls of 10 to 20 mm about the Lower South East district and with thunderstorms.
